subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB329 (LANDED 2026-09-05). RULE: 'If the execution of the READ statement is successful but the record area contains one or more characters not in the implementor-defined character set for a line sequential file, the I-O status in the read file connector is set to 09.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the record area contains one or more characters not in the implementor-defined character set for a line sequential file' -> OK 14.9.30.4 16); cite.py --check 9.1.13.2 'A READ statement for a line sequential file has successfully executed but the record contains one or more characters that are not in the implementor-defined character set for a line sequential file' -> OK 9.1.13.2 7). WHAT THE RULE DELEGATES TO IS NOW DETERMINED: Annex A.1 item 115 (Line sequential character set, required + documented) is answered at docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-115 -- every character at or above U+0020 is a member, the C0 controls below it (CR, LF and HT included) are not -- and LineSequentialCharacterSet is its one executable copy. SequentialConnector.Read's line-sequential arm tests the DELIVERED record area through the shared predicate and ReadSucceeded lands 09 ahead of 06/04, because GR16 is stated after GR15 and asks only that the read be successful. The test is CHARACTER-wise, not byte-wise: a national record area is read two bytes at a time as UTF-16BE (14.9.30.4 GR15's own alphanumeric/national split, D-N1), so N"CD"'s 00 43 00 44 bytes are two members and not two control characters. MEASURED on the built cobol.exe: before, a line sequential READ of a line holding 0x00 reported STATUS=00; after, 09, with the record still delivered (FUNCTION ORD of the byte = 1). Goldens walk 09 (READ), 71 (WRITE, 14.9.51.4 GR23), 71 (REWRITE, 14.9.35.4 GR17d), 9.1.13.10 item 1's unchanged medium, and the set boundary (0x7F and 0xFF are members) at 2023, the one edition the organization exists in. kb/Work PB688 (2026-09-05): ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL is a COBOL-2023 INTRODUCTION - the Foreword's list of the main changes this third edition makes over ISO/IEC 1989:2014 names "Line Sequential file organization", and 9.1.6 / 9.1.7.1 still name exactly three organizations with 9.1.7.2 splitting the sequential one into its record- and line-delimited types. The organization therefore does not exist below 2023 (the pass now rejects it with COBOL0900, registry row file-organization-line-sequential-2023), the 2002 and 2014 copies of the golden were deleted as programs no edition below 2023 can express, and this row's editions are 2023 alone.
